source.text: ወዲበ፡ ውእቱ፡ ንቅዐት፡ ርኢኩ፡ መካነ፡ ወ*ኢጽገበ፡ ሰማይ፡ ላዕሌሁ፡ ወኢመሰረተ፡ ምድር፡ በታሕቴሁ፡ ወኢማን፡ አልቦ፡ በላዕሌሁ፡ ወኢአዕዋፈ፡ እላ፡ መካነ፡ ባድው፡ ውእቱ፡ ወገሩም።
source.note: Charles1906 printed50/PDF88, completeunit12 beforemarker13. Diplomatic main-text water-position token ends in nunን and is preserved asወኢማን; English water follows the disclosed reading reported by this edition’s apparatus17, not a silent main-text glyph normalization. Actualnegative*ኢ retained. Apparatusnumerals suppressed,punctuationnormalized. No independent manuscript or human-specialist certification.

translation.text: Beyond that chasm[a] I saw a place with no heaven covering it above,[b] and no foundation of earth beneath it. There was no water above it[c] and no birds; it was an empty and terrifying place.

footnotes.text: Beyond renders the contextual direction; the printed Ge’ez preposition is literally on/upon. Charles calls it a wrong rendering of the Greek beyond in printed50 note13. This follows that disclosed editorial explanation, not an independently collated Greek manuscript.

The selected print has the marked negativeኢ before the heaven-covering verb. Charles’s printed50 note14 records its omission by witnessq; this translation retains the selected negative rather than silently changing it to a positive.

The selected main printing hasማን, ending with the nun-shaped letterን, not the ordinary finalይ of the water-word. This source record preserves that anomalous printing. English water follows the water-reading reported in Charles’s printed50 note17; Dillmann’s1865 lexicon,column212,gives aqua for the water-word. Whether the main printed anomaly is a typesetting error or reflects an antecedent cannot be established from these images. The apparatus reports manuscript readings; those manuscripts were not independently inspected here.
